acceptance_mapping.no_restart_ignores_consumed_attempt_or_h: I3 + OC-7 + OC-11 + OC-12 (model traces T1, T1b, T6, T7)
acceptance_mapping.no_two_transport_calls_per_symbol_captur: I1 + I2 + OC-5 F-PRECALL + OC-7/OC-8 (model traces T1, T1b, T2, T5, T6)

clauses.OC-1: Identity object created per objects.identity_object before the first ATTEMPT; missing/unreadable object at open -> HOLD:IDENTITY_MISSING; binding mismatch -> HOLD:IDENTITY_MISMATCH.
clauses.OC-10: No pathname cleanup: the executor performs NO unlink/rename of any dirent except the OC-9 no-replace rename of its own verified temp. Temps/finals that fail identity proof are abandoned in place (nonce-named evidence for the sealing census, which HOLDs on non-members). Deletion of any capture artifact is out-of-band and separately authorized — never an executor behavior.
clauses.OC-11: Single durability route: every post-ATTEMPT failure of any class (transport, serialization, ceiling, filesystem, fence, finalize, path) appends exactly one schema-strict HOLD record (capture_id, symbol-or-null, code, detail, attempt-consumed flag) via the held journal fd + fsync before returning. If that append itself fails -> return HOLD:JOURNAL_DURABILITY and do NOT claim the cause was recorded. Restart semantics unchanged: ATTEMPT without COMPLETE -> HOLD:ATTEMPT_CONSUMED_AMBIGUOUS, zero calls.
clauses.OC-12: Identity is never (dev,ino) alone: every trust decision requires nonce + genesis_hash + chain continuity in addition to (dev,ino), so a recycled inode number presenting a forged genesis fails as HOLD:JOURNAL_REPLACED.
clauses.OC-2: Journal record 0 is GENESIS binding capture_id + nonce + the journal's own (dev,ino) + control (dev,ino); its hash is carried in the identity object and re-verified at every open/resolve.
clauses.OC-3: Hash chain + exact-key schema validation on every record at open/resolve; any break, extra/missing key, or seq gap -> HOLD:JOURNAL_CORRUPT or HOLD:JOURNAL_CONFLICT; recomputation verifies, it never corrects a record.
clauses.OC-4: All opens are fd-relative: trusted parent -> component-wise O_NOFOLLOW walk -> pinned control-dir fd -> flock -> openat(journal, O_NOFOLLOW) exactly once. The journal is never reopened by pathname; every append uses the held fd; every record's run binds the fd's (dev,ino).
clauses.OC-5: Fence points: F-OPEN (before journal read), F-APPEND (before ATTEMPT append), F-PRECALL (after ATTEMPT fsync, immediately before the transport call), F-FINALIZE (before the no-replace rename), F-COMPLETE (before COMPLETE append). Each fence checks: (i) pinned dir fd identity unchanged; (ii) journal name lookup within the pinned dir fd resolves to the held journal fd's (dev,ino); (iii) control-dir name lookup in the parent resolves to the pinned control fd's (dev,ino); (iv) identity object re-read equals the open-time binding.
clauses.OC-6: Fence failure: append the named HOLD via the single durability route (OC-11) onto the held journal fd, fsync, exit. Never call transport after any fence failure in the run. Live-detection never substitutes for restart resolution (OC-7).
clauses.OC-7: Restart resolution algorithm: read identity object -> resolve control dir by binding (canonical name if its (dev,ino) equals the binding; else scan the archive parent's entries for the binding inode -> found renamed: HOLD:JOURNAL_RENAMED after locating the journal inside it; not found: HOLD:CONTROL_REPLACED) -> resolve journal name inside the control dir: (dev,ino) equals binding and genesis+chain verify (OC-2/OC-3, including nonce — (dev,ino) alone NEVER suffices, OC-12) -> proceed from verified records; name is a symlink -> HOLD:PATH_TYPE; name binds a different inode -> scan control-dir entries for the binding inode: found under another name -> HOLD:JOURNAL_RENAMED; not found -> HOLD:JOURNAL_REPLACED; empty file -> no GENESIS -> HOLD:JOURNAL_REPLACED.
clauses.OC-8: Single owner per I1: contender finding the dir-fd flock held -> HOLD:OWNER_BUSY, zero transport calls, zero journal mutation. No age-based takeover; a dead owner's lock releases only via the OS on fd close, and the successor still passes OC-7 before any call.
clauses.OC-9: Publication: temp created O_EXCL under an attempt-unique nonce name and held open; F-FINALIZE re-opens the temp NAME fd-relatively and requires its (dev,ino) to equal the held temp fd (mismatch -> HOLD:TEMP_SUBSTITUTED, abandon per OC-10); renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) within the member dir fd (destination raced -> HOLD:FINAL_COLLISION, destination bytes untouched); F-COMPLETE re-opens the final name and requires (dev,ino) == temp identity AND content hash == recorded payload hash (mismatch -> HOLD:FINAL_SUBSTITUTED, NO COMPLETE). COMPLETE binds the final's (dev,ino) + hash.

invariants.I1_single_transport_owner: At most one live process may reach a transport call for a capture. Ownership = holding flock on the pinned control-dir fd; there is no lock FILE and no pathname lock object anywhere.
invariants.I2_attempt_immediately_precedes_call: The only statements permitted between ATTEMPT append+fsync and the transport call are the F-PRECALL fence (OC-5) and the call itself. A fence failure in that window means the call MUST NOT happen, and the consumed ATTEMPT stands.
invariants.I3_durable_reachable_restart_truth: Restart truth is resolved from the identity object (OC-7), never from the canonical pathname alone. No code path may treat an unverified, empty, copied, or recycled journal as fresh history. A consumed ATTEMPT or HOLD in the true journal binds every later process.
invariants.I4_fencing_after_replacement: Replacement of the journal name, the control-dir name, or the identity object — live or across exit — fences the owner out (live: OC-6; restart: OC-7). Fencing is a property of identity comparison, not of the flock: the flock excludes cooperative contenders only while the owner lives.
invariants.I5_publication_identity: COMPLETE may be appended only for a final whose (dev,ino) AND content hash are re-verified at F-COMPLETE to equal the held temp fd's identity and the recorded payload hash. The executor NEVER unlinks or renames a dirent it cannot prove is its own via a currently held fd; unprovable dirents are abandoned in place as evidence (OC-10).

objects.control_dir_fd: pinned directory fd obtained by component-wise O_NOFOLLOW traversal from the documented trusted parent; flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on THIS fd is the only ownership token

identity_object.creation: O_EXCL write-once at capture setup; fsync file + fsync parent dir before any ATTEMPT
identity_object.location: archive parent directory (OUTSIDE the control directory, OUTSIDE the capture root)
identity_object.mutability: immutable; superseded only by a separately authorized recovery act that creates a NEW versioned object (never an edit)
identity_object.name: <capture_id>.identity.json

journal.chain: every record carries seq + prev_hash + hash (hash-chained, exact-key schemas per r3)
journal.location: <capture_id>.control/ (sibling of the capture root, per the -18 r2 membership contract)
journal.name: acquisition_attempt_journal.qfj2

platform_assumptions: Linux local filesystem (ext4-class) for the archive tree: flock(2) advisory semantics, fsync durability, renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE), openat/O_NOFOLLOW per-component traversal. NFS or any network filesystem is OUT of assumption (flock/fsync/identity semantics differ) — the capture tree is local disk on this VM.
(dev,ino) is stable for the life of an inode on one filesystem and unique among LIVE inodes; it is explicitly NOT trusted across free/realloc (hence OC-12).

The adversary model is accidental-or-hostile LOCAL pathname manipulation between syscalls (the lineage's demonstrated threat: races, swaps, stale copies), not a compromised kernel or an attacker who can write the identity object before setup completes; setup itself runs before the capture is announced.
One archive tree per capture executor host; cross-host ownership is out of scope.
purpose: Minimal persistent-ownership contract for the clean capture executor such that journal/control pathname replacement — including across owner exit — can never produce a second transport call, a lost consumed ATTEMPT/HOLD, a foreign unlink, or a COMPLETE bound to a replaced final.

recovery.R-1_OWNER_BUSY: Wait for the live owner; no action, no takeover.
recovery.R-2_JOURNAL_RENAMED_or_CONTROL_REPLACED_: Out-of-band, separately authorized: verify the located inode's genesis+nonce+chain against the identity object; if authentic, append a REBIND record to the true journal and issue a NEW versioned identity object naming the restored canonical layout. The executor never rebinds by itself. Until rebound, the capture makes no calls.
recovery.R-3_JOURNAL_REPLACED_not_located: The capture is dead. Consumed attempts stand consumed; any retry is a NEW capture_id under a new identity object. No resurrection from the replacement file, however plausible its contents.
recovery.R-4_JOURNAL_DURABILITY: Treat every attempt of the affected run as consumed-ambiguous; the capture HOLDs until R-2/R-3 disposition.
